name: The Mask
summary: Dark Horse's cursed jade mask, which turns anyone who wears it into the green-headed, reality-bending maniac Big Head. Far gorier on the page than in Jim Carrey's 1994 film.
origin: The Mask is a semi-living ancient jade mask. Its first victim in the comics is Stanley Ipkiss, a meek man full of grudges who buys it in an antiques shop as a gift. Wearing it, he turns into a bald, green-headed creature with huge teeth and almost limitless power, and goes on a revenge spree the press calls Big Head. The mask strips away all inhibitions, so every wearer ends up a violent antihero or villain, whatever they intended. Stanley is shot dead by his girlfriend Kathy wearing the mask herself, and it soon passes to police lieutenant Mitch Kellaway.
powers: Cartoonish transformations of body and surroundings
Removes the wearer's inhibitions, and often their sanity

storyline.title: A sketch for APA-5
storyline.beat: Mike Richardson comes up with the idea in 1982 and draws a sketch for an amateur press publication in 1985.

storyline.title: Masque
storyline.beat: Mark Badger's Masque strip runs in early Dark Horse Presents, but it turns political and Richardson ends it.

storyline.title: Mayhem
storyline.beat: Chris Warner redesigns the character, and John Arcudi and Doug Mahnke's stories in Mayhem #1–4 make it a hit.

storyline.title: Big Head's rampage
storyline.beat: A four-issue series follows the mask from Stanley to Kellaway and introduces the silent mob enforcer Walter.

storyline.title: Jim Carrey
storyline.beat: The film loosely adapts the first half of the Arcudi/Mahnke series and turns the gore into slapstick.

storyline.title: Joker/Mask
storyline.beat: Team-ups and fights include Lobo/Mask. The run closes in 2000 with Joker/Mask, in which the Joker gets hold of the mask.

storyline.title: I Pledge Allegiance to the Mask!
storyline.beat: The mask returns in a new series, alongside the kid-friendly spin-off Itty Bitty Mask.

gossip.text: In the early comics the character was called Big Head. 'The Mask' meant the object, and the name only stuck to the character thanks to the film and cartoon.
The Mask was always a goofy comedy.
gossip.truth: The original comics are violent comedy-horror. Big Head kills police officers and the stories are notoriously graphic.

gossip.text: Its inspirations include the Joker, the Green Goblin, Freddy Krueger, Jekyll and Hyde, and Steve Ditko's Creeper.
Executive producer Michael De Luca suggested Jim Carrey, and that casting helped push the film toward comedy.
Mike Richardson came up with the concept on 5 February 1982, before Dark Horse Comics existed.

quiz.q: What was the masked character called in the early comics?
quiz.why: The press nicknamed the green-headed wearer Big Head.

quiz.q: Who is the first wearer of the Mask in the comics?
quiz.why: Stanley buys it as a gift in an antiques shop.

quiz.q: Which DC villain gets the Mask in a 2000 crossover?
quiz.why: Joker/Mask puts the mask on Batman's archenemy.

theme.tagline: Put it on and your conscience takes the week off.

timeline.title: Mayhem #1
timeline.note: Chris Warner's redesign turns the cursed mask into Big Head, and Arcudi and Mahnke's stories make it a hit.

timeline.title: The Mask miniseries
timeline.note: A four-issue run introduces Stanley Ipkiss, the mute hitman Walter and the dogged Lieutenant Kellaway.

timeline.title: Jim Carrey's The Mask
timeline.note: The July 1994 film swaps the comic's gore for cartoon slapstick and turns Big Head into a star.

timeline.title: Animated series
timeline.note: The Mask: Animated Series spins the film's lighter take into TV cartoons through 1997.

timeline.title: Joker/Mask
timeline.note: In a crossover with DC, the Joker gets his hands on the mask.

timeline.title: Son of the Mask
timeline.note: A film sequel without Carrey follows a new family dealing with the mask.

timeline.title: I Pledge Allegiance to the Mask!
timeline.note: The main comic comes back with the mask tangled up in a presidential race.
